action_history.rationale: Approach: Convert to physical volts, put the image on square pixels and remove the instrument tilt, then cluster the leveled surface potential into contact-potential domains and quantify their CPD contrast in mV and their area fractions.

result.detailed_analysis:
The KPFM contact potential difference (CPD) map of a multi-layer hBN van der Waals stack was converted to volts, resampled to square pixels (19.53 nm/px, 10x10 um field of view), and leveled (per-row 1st-order polynomial + plane subtraction) to remove scanner drift and slow tilt. The residual stripe std after row-alignment (~2.3 mV) is small relative to the total leveled potential range (~104 mV), indicating the leveling successfully suppressed line-to-line offset artifacts without erasing the real surface-potential signal. Only 0.36% of pixels were masked as artifacts (a localized topographic/probe scarring feature in the upper-left, coincident with the bright diagonal ridge in the topography), so the clustering operated on essentially the full valid field.

Adaptive K-means partitioned the leveled potential into two spatially-coherent CPD domains with mean potentials of -10.5 mV (domain 1, 35% of area) and +5.9 mV (domain 2, 65% of area), a pairwise contrast of ~16 mV. Physically, these two populations correspond to regions of differing effective work function / surface potential on the hBN surface — most plausibly areas of differing layer number (thickness terraces) or differing dielectric/charge screening, since work function in few-layer 2D materials depends on layer count and substrate coupling. The more-negative domain forms the connected diagonal band running lower-left to upper region (following the topographic terracing), while the more-positive domain occupies the broad lower-right majority. The within-domain std (~6-8 mV) is comparable to the inter-domain contrast, so the two populations are only weakly separated — consistent with the map being closer to a smooth CPD gradient than to sharply bounded discrete domains.

Importantly, the domain-count selection is not robust: silhouette (0.558) and BIC (-1.558e6) both favor k=3, and only the largest-connected-component coherence criterion favors k=2. This means the true CPD landscape likely contains three (or a continuum of) potential levels, and forcing k=2 collapses a gradient into two bins. Consequently the reported ~16 mV contrast should be treated as a lower bound; the full leveled range of ~104 mV is the more honest measure of the total surface-potential heterogeneity across the flake.

scientific_claims.claim: The hBN surface exhibits spatially-coherent surface-potential heterogeneity with a total leveled CPD range of ~104 mV, organized into at least two work-function domains (mean CPD -10.5 mV over 35% of area vs +5.9 mV over 65% of area; pairwise contrast ~16 mV).
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Spatially-correlated CPD domains in multi-layer hBN reveal layer-number- and substrate-coupling-dependent work-function variation, which governs charge injection, dielectric screening, and interfacial band alignment in vdW heterostructure devices. Mapping these domains connects local layer terracing to electrostatic potential landscape.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone observed layer-dependent contact-potential-difference domains in multi-layer hBN with inter-domain contrast on the order of tens of mV using Kelvin probe force microscopy?

result.analysis_approach: Convert to physical volts, put the image on square pixels and remove the instrument tilt, then cluster the leveled surface potential into contact-potential domains and quantify their CPD contrast in mV and their area fractions.

issues.problem: Silhouette (0.558) and BIC (most negative, -1.558e6) both favor k=3, but k=2 was selected on the basis of coherence. The reported rationale ('silhouette + BIC + coherence') is somewhat inconsistent since two of the three metrics point to k=3.

Reported CPD contrast between the two domains is only ~16 mV, which is at the low end for KPFM and much smaller than the total leveled potential range (~104 mV). A 2-cluster split of a continuous gradient tends to under-report true domain contrast.
